question: A 72-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of blurry vision for the past 3 days. He has also had 4 episodes of right-sided headaches over the past month. He has no significant past medical history. His father died of coronary artery disease at the age of 62 years. His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 94/min, and blood pressure is 232/128 mm Hg. Fundoscopy shows right-sided optic disc blurring and retinal hemorrhages. A medication is given immediately. Five minutes later, his pulse is 75/min and blood pressure is 190/105 mm Hg. Which of the following drugs was most likely administered?
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms suggestive of hypertensive emergency with hypertensive retinopathy. The initial high blood pressure and symptoms indicate the need for rapid blood pressure reduction. The drug most likely administered in this scenario is a fast-acting antihypertensive agent.
